## Rule (the layering principle)

Four distinct enforcement layers, and **type/model validity is not in the layer you'd expect**:

| Layer | What it enforces | Mechanism |
|---|---|---|
| HTTP/route (reitit + clojure.spec) | *shape only*: `typeId` matches `p[0-9]+` (`::specs/componentType`), reference `:type` is `int?`, required keys, string limits | route `:parameters {:body ...}` + `coerce-request-middleware` |
| API resource (liberator) | *entity-level model invariants*, via `:processable?` → `crud-service/processable?` | `src/ardoq/api/crud_api_v2.clj:241-243,304-305,346-349,383-397` |
| Service | *field-value* validity/coercion, type resolution, reference endpoint checks | `model-service/ensure-valid-fields-many!`, `model-service/resolve-component-types!`, `reference-service/validate-many` |
| Persistence | *spec re-check only* (`entity/ensure-valid!` against `:spec` of the repo config). **Zero model awareness.** | `src/ardoq/persistence/postgres_entity.clj:15-20,51,71,98,131` |

**There is no single "validate entity against model" chokepoint.** The closest thing is the `crud-service/processable?` / `every-processable?` multimethod pair (`src/ardoq/service/crud_service.clj:51-65`), dispatched per service. It is invoked **only from liberator `:processable?` callbacks in the API layer** — `component-service/create!`/`update!` and `reference-service/create!`/`update!` never call it (`src/ardoq/service/component_service.clj:640-652,716-726`; `reference_service.clj:203-210,234-241`). Any internal/service-layer caller therefore bypasses all model-hierarchy and type-legality validation. Field-value validation is the opposite: it lives inside the service write functions and cannot be bypassed from the API.

## 1. Component create/update — is `:typeId`/`:type`/`:componentTypeId` validated?

**`:typeId` — yes, in the API-layer `:processable?` gate.**
`crud-service/every-processable? :component-service` (`component_service.clj:530-570`) → `processable-operation?` (`:414-481`) → `model-util/legal-hierarchy-error` (`src/ardoq/utils/model_utils.clj:519-542`) → `legal-hierarchy?` (`:437-444`). The model is fetched from the component's `rootWorkspace` → `:componentModel`, then `model-adapter/transmute`d (`component_service.clj:538-543`).

- Create: order is `:parent` exists (`:424-427`) → model resolvable (`:429-432`) → cycle check (`circular-hierarchy-as-client-error`, `:389-395`) → `legal-hierarchy-error`.
- Update: immutability (`rootWorkspace`, `component-key` — `:327-346`) → model resolvable → parent exists → `(not= (:model parent) (:model new-entity))` → self-parent → cycle → `legal-hierarchy-error`.
- All failures are `client-utils/error` → 422 (`crud_api_v2.clj:260-266`).

**Unknown type → 422, never silent accept, never auto-create-type.** In a strict model `legal-hierarchy?` requires the id to be in the parent's (or root's) declared children set; in a flexible model it requires `legal-type?`, i.e. presence in `(:metadata transmuted-model)` (`model_utils.clj:398-402`).

**Missing `:typeId` on create → auto-assigned, not rejected.** `legal-hierarchy?` returns true when `component-type-id` is nil. Then in the service, `model-service/resolve-component-types!` (`model_service.clj:183-186`) → `model-util/resolve-component-type` (`model_utils.clj:411-425`) picks the *first* type from `available-types` for the parent, logging `"Assigning random type to component"` when more than one is possible, or throws `::client-utils/no-available-child-type`. If a `:typeId` is present it is re-checked against `(-> metadata keys set)`; a miss yields `nil` → `util/ensure!` → bare `ex-info` (500), reachable only by callers that skipped `processable?`.

**`:type` (type name) is server-derived and never persisted.** `resolve-component-types` sets both `:typeId` and `:type` from the model on create; `component_repo/pre-write` → `remove-deps` drops `:type` before the insert (`src/ardoq/persistence/component_repo.clj:140-143,187-193`); it is re-attached on read by `component-deps/assoc-deps!`. Note: `bulk-update-sans-events!` does **not** call `resolve-component-types!` (`component_service.clj:696-714`), so on update `:type` is simply discarded and `:typeId` is trusted after the `processable?` check.

**`:componentTypeId`** — a nullable, `DEFERRABLE INITIALLY DEFERRED` FK to `component_type._id` (`resources/migrations/org_db_sqls/add-component-componentTypeId-fk.sql`), accepted by the spec (`component_repo.clj:97,114`) but **set by nothing in the write paths**. The only writer is `migration/core/global_types.clj:91-102`, which has no caller in `src` (verified by `git grep componentTypeId origin/master -- src`). Type identity at write time is the `(model, typeId)` pair.

## 2. Reference create/update

**`:type` against the model's `:referenceTypes` — yes**, in `reference-service/ensure-good-reference-type!` (`reference_service.clj:271-274`), called from `processable?*` (`:289-308`) under `every-processable? :reference-service` (`:310-334`). Miss → throws `::client-utils/bad-reference-type` (not a returned error — an exception).

**Model resolved from the SOURCE workspace.** `every-processable?` collects the sources (`:source` of `:entity` on create, of `:new-entity` on update), reads `source.rootWorkspace` → workspace `:componentModel` → model (`:312-328`). Also enforced: `ensure-good-root-workspace-and-model!` (`:276-287`) rejects a payload whose `:rootWorkspace` or `:model` differs from the source component's. `targetWorkspace` may differ freely — that is how cross-workspace references work; the target's own model is never consulted. In the service, `validate-many` (`:122-131`) additionally requires both endpoints to exist (`::reference-endpoint-missing`, `:90-120`) and *overwrites* `:rootWorkspace`/`:model` from the source and `:targetWorkspace` from the target (`:79-83`).

**Source/target component types are NOT checked.** There is no triple/endpoint-type constraint anywhere on this path — the model document has no source-type/target-type structure for reference types (`model_utils.clj:109-110,230-237`), and `processable?*` plus `validate-many`/`add-model-many` (the complete set of reference write-path validators, read in full) contain no component-type lookup. The `:triples` in `metamodel-service-v2` are usage statistics consumed by `sorted-most-used-ref-types` (`reference_service.clj:521-565`), not a constraint.

`reference.referenceTypeId` has the same never-populated FK situation as `componentTypeId` (`migration/core/global_types.clj:104-115`).

## 3. Field values on components/references

**One entry point, used on both create and update, for both entity kinds:** `model-service/ensure-valid-fields-many!` (`model_service.clj:164-174`) — called at `component_service.clj:614` (create), `:708` (update), `reference_service.clj:187` (create), `:227` (update).

It loads `field` rows by the entity's `:model` (`model_service.clj:158-162`), then per entity:
1. `field-utils/ensure-read-only-fields-don't-change!` (`field_utils.clj:571-574`) — **silently overwrites** submitted values for *calculated* fields (those with `:calculatedFieldSettings.storedQueryId`) with the stored values. Locally-derived fields are not covered here.
2. Filters to `field-utils/applicable?` (`model_service.clj:146-149`; `field_utils.clj:195-204`) — a field applies iff the entity's `:typeId` is in the field's `:componentType` vector, or the reference's `:type` is in `:referenceType`. **This is where "which component types the field applies to" is enforced**: a value for a field that exists in the model but is not applied to this type is not coerced, not typechecked, and is stored as an opaque custom-field value.
3. `field-utils/ensure-valid-fields!` (`field_utils.clj:593-607`): reject keys containing `.` → `coerce` → `typecheck!` → `initialize-missing-fields`.

**Coercion by declared field `:type` — yes**, `coerced-field-value` (`field_utils.clj:409-451`): strings→`str`, `->number`, ISO parse for `Date`/`DateTime`, `->boolean` for `Checkbox`, case-insensitive option matching for `List`/`SelectMultipleList`. A failed coercion returns the original value so the typecheck produces a client error.

**Type check** — `typecheck!` (`:469-480`) → `-typecheck!` (`:371-393`) → the `checker` multimethod (`:307-350`, per field type, incl. `List` membership and text-size limits) → throws `::client-utils/invalid-list-field-value` or `::client-utils/invalid-attribute`.

**`defaultValue`** — only used to fill *absent* fields (`initialize-missing-fields`, `:489-505`), and skipped for list types (`default-value-for-field`, `:482-487`). It is never enforced as a constraint on submitted values.

**"Required" fields do not exist.** `field_repo`'s entity spec has no required/mandatory attribute (`src/ardoq/persistence/field_repo.clj:44-56`), and nothing in `ensure-valid-fields!` can reject a missing value — it fills the default instead. Verified by reading the full field spec and the whole `ensure-valid-fields!` chain.

**Undeclared field key → silently stored.** `typecheck!` skips keys with no matching field; `component_repo/pre-write` → `repo/gather-custom-fields` moves every key outside `non-custom-fields` into the `__ardoqCustomFields` jsonb column (`component_repo.clj:162-193`). Only a `.` in the key is rejected (`field_utils.clj:582-591`).

## 4. Component-type / reference-type / field *definition* writes

**Component types and reference types have no write API of their own** — `component_type_api.clj:56` and `reference_type_api.clj:56` mount `crud-v3/read-only-api`. Type rows are derived: `model-service/update!` fires `::hook-service/after-model-but-before-types-updated`, and `component-type-service/update-component-types!` / `reference-type-service/update-reference-types!` diff the old and new model root and create/update/delete rows (`component_type_service.clj:109-127,129-150`; `reference_type_service.clj:93-111,113-134`). `component-type-service/bulk-create!`/`bulk-update!`/`bulk-delete!` (`:56-100`) go the other way — they rebuild the model root and call `model-service/update!` — so **every type invariant is a model invariant**.

`model-service/update!` (`model_service.clj:390-404`) enforces, in order:
- `verify-valid-model-change` (`:118-125`, `:109-116`) — a removed component type that still has components → 422 `::invalid-model` with `"cannot-delete"` per type (**type-in-use-on-delete**).
- `model-util/validate-model` (`model_utils.clj:489-517`) — no blank component/reference type names; no type name starting with `~` (Gremlin label restriction, ARD-23989).
- `validate-component-type-images!` (`model_service.clj:369-388`) — no foreign-workspace image URIs.

and via `crud-service/processable? :model-service` (`:304-319`, on the PUT path only):
- `validate-flexibility` (`:226-241`) — see §5.
- `validate-removal-of-reference-types` (`:204-208`) — reference types still in use cannot be removed.
- `validate-adding-reference-type` (`:212-224`) — a newly added reference type's key must equal `maxReferenceTypeKey`.
- `validate-consistent-type-ids` (`:243-263`) — every `:referenceTypes`/`:root` map key must equal the entry's `:id`.

**Type name uniqueness is NOT enforced on `PUT /api/model/:id`.** `validate-model` checks blankness and the `~` prefix only; `unique-type-names!` (`:440-444`) is a query, not a validator. Duplicate component-type *names* within a model are only rejected on the metamodel-sync path: `metamodel-sync-service/processable?` (`src/ardoq/service/metamodel_sync_service.clj:151-217`) rejects duplicate component-type names, duplicate reference-type names, duplicate field names, deleting all component types, deleting a type still referenced by a field or used as another type's `:parent`, and `invalid-parent-child-component-type-hierarchy` (a cycle among `:parent` links). `PUT /api/model/:id` also does not reject a type appearing twice in the hierarchy — `bad-type-hierarchy?` (`model_utils.clj:197-210`) is used only by the nightly integrity check.

**Field definitions.** Create is `POST /api/field` (`field_api.clj:25-53,249-253`) → `field-service/processable?` (`field_service.clj:856-859` → `every-processable?` `:824-854` → `processable*?` `:802-822`):
- create: `validate-type` (no duplicate list options, `:679-684`) → `validate-attribute-name` (non-blank, matches `attribute-name-re`, not `_`-prefixed, not a reserved attribute name — `:369-414`; skipped if a same-named sibling field already exists, a deliberate legacy escape hatch) → `unique-attribute-name?` (no other field in the same model with the same derived name, `:548-559`) → `validate-model-exists` → calculated-field-settings validation → `validate-that-default-value-matches-type` (`:716-729`).
- update: `defaultValue` must still match `:type`, and `:name`, `:type`, `:label`, `:model` are **immutable** (`update-allowed?`, `:773-800`).
- plus `ensure-global-field-invariant!` (`:603-618`) in `bulk-create!`, which forces cross-model global-field consistency and throws `field-conflict` errors.
- **Non-existent type ids in `:componentType`/`:referenceType` are silently dropped, not rejected** — `remove-non-existing-types!` (`:202-205`) is applied in the create (`:984`) and update (`:1066`) pipelines.
- There is **no single-entity field update or delete HTTP route**: `field_api.clj` exposes only `POST ""` plus read/command endpoints. Field definition updates/deletes go through `metamodel_sync_api.clj` (`sync-metamodel`, `update-global-field`, `delete-global-field`).

## 5. Parent/child and the `:flexible` flag

Yes, `:parent` is validated against the type hierarchy, in `model-util/legal-hierarchy?` (`model_utils.clj:437-444`), reached from `legal-hierarchy-error` on both component create and update. `:flexible` is read in exactly two places on this path:

```clojure
;; model_utils.clj:404-409
(defn- available-types [{:keys [component-hierarchy flexible]} parent-type-id]
  (if-let [strict-available (get component-hierarchy (or parent-type-id "root"))]
    strict-available
    (when flexible (get component-hierarchy "root"))))

;; model_utils.clj:437-444
(defn legal-hierarchy? [transmuted-model parent-type-id component-type-id]
  (boolean (if (:flexible transmuted-model)
             (or (not component-type-id) (legal-type? transmuted-model component-type-id))
             (let [available? (available-types transmuted-model parent-type-id)]
               (when (seq available?)
                 (or (not component-type-id) (available? component-type-id)))))))
```

**Exactly what `:flexible` gates:** it replaces the parent-child pairing check with a bare "does this type exist in the model" check. In a flexible model any type may be a child of any type (or top-level); in a strict model the component's type must be in the parent type's declared `:children` set (or, with no parent, in the root set), and a parent type with no declared children admits no children at all. The second reader (`available-types`) only affects type *auto-assignment* when `:typeId` is absent: for a flexible model an unknown parent type falls back to the root-level types.

`:flexible` cannot be turned off while violations exist: `model-service/validate-flexibility` (`model_service.clj:226-241`) runs `model-util/component-hierarchy-violations` (`model_utils.clj:544-556`) over every component in the workspace on a `flexible: true → false` model update and returns `::model-cannot-be-converted-to-rigid`. The reverse direction is unchecked.

Also enforced on parents: cycles (`fetch-hierarchies!` + Tarjan SCC → `::grandfather-paradox`, `component_service.clj:389-395,483-507,556-561`), self-parent, parent must exist, and on update parent must share the component's `:model`.

`model-util/validate-component-hierarchy` / `ensure-valid-component-hierarchy!` (`model_utils.clj:451-487`) are a **separate, parallel implementation** used only by the surveys code (`src/ardoq/surveys/payload/validation.clj:47,106-107`; `src/ardoq/surveys/validation/survey.clj:98`); `ensure-valid-component-hierarchy!` has no caller in `src` at all.

## 6. `model_integrity_checks.clj` — on-demand only, never on writes

It is a *detection* namespace, not enforcement. `run-integrity-checks!` (`model_integrity_checks.clj:241-304`) returns a vector of `{:description :passed? :stable? :data}` maps; it is called only from the nightly per-org integrity job / `integrity-service/lint!` (`src/ardoq/service/integrity_check_registry.clj` docstring; `branch_integrity_checks.clj:48-49` for branches). No write path references it (`git grep run-integrity-checks! origin/master -- src`).

What it checks: `model.root` hierarchy consistency (`bad-type-hierarchy?`), every non-template model has a workspace, `model.root` ↔ `component_type` table agreement both ways plus attribute-level divergence and `:parent` mismatches, same for `model.referenceTypes` ↔ `reference_type`, every model has an `Implicit` reference type with id 2, component-type image URIs and colors, and valid `lineBeginning`/`lineEnding` arrow types on reference types and model templates.

Its siblings: `component_integrity_checks.clj:223-289` verifies exactly the invariants the write path *doesn't* — `component.{model,typeId}` resolves against the model and against `component_type`, `componentTypeId` non-null and FK-consistent, parent exists in the same model, no parent cycles, no self-parent, list-field values adhere to options. `reference_integrity_checks.clj:109-133` likewise checks `reference.{model,type}` against the model and `reference_type`, `rootWorkspace == source.rootWorkspace`, `targetWorkspace == target.rootWorkspace`, and `referenceTypeId`. `field_integrity_checks.clj:173-227` covers field-definition hygiene (whitespace, cyclic derived fields, reactive fields reading confidential fields, unapplied workspace fields).

## Explicit non-enforcement (and how verified)

- **Reference endpoint component types** — no constraint exists. Verified by reading the complete reference write path: `reference_api.clj` (crud-v3 routes) → `crud_api_v2.clj:293-311,335-361` → `crud-service/processable? :reference-service` → `processable?*`/`every-processable?` (`reference_service.clj:289-334`) → `bulk-create-sans-events!`/`bulk-update-sans-events!` (`:180-232`).
- **Field "required"** — no such attribute. Verified against `field_repo.clj:44-56` and `field_utils.clj:593-607`.
- **Values for undeclared or inapplicable field keys** — accepted and stored in the custom-fields jsonb. Verified in `field_utils.clj:469-480` (typecheck skips) and `component_repo.clj:162-193` (`gather-custom-fields`).
- **Duplicate type names on `PUT /api/model/:id`** — not rejected. Verified by reading `model-service/update!` and `model-util/validate-model` in full.
- **`componentTypeId`/`referenceTypeId` FK population** — no write path sets them. Verified by `git grep` over `origin/master:src`.
